title: Decoder: One-Hot Outputs and Function Implementation
quickIdea: An n-to-2^n decoder turns an n-bit code into exactly one active output line, so its outputs are the 2^n minterms of the inputs. OR the outputs for the 1s and you have built the function.
remember: n inputs, 2^n outputs, exactly one output active for each input code. Output k is active when the input code is k.
Active-high decoder: Y_k = minterm k. Active-low decoder: Y_k = (minterm k)' = maxterm k.
Function implementation: OR the minterm outputs that the function needs. With an active-low decoder the same function is a NAND of the selected outputs, because each output is already complemented.
An enable input makes every output inactive when it is off; that is how decoders are cascaded - a small decoder on the top address bits enables one of several bigger ones.
A decoder followed by a set of OR gates is a look-up table: n inputs, 2^n minterms, m OR gates give m functions of the same n variables.
A counter feeding a decoder produces a one-hot sequence, which is a ring counter - GATE CSE 2014 Set 2 Q.7 turns on exactly that observation.
A demultiplexer is a decoder whose enable has become the data input; that is why the two are the same circuit.

example.prompt: Implement f(A,B) = m1 + m2 with a 2-to-4 decoder and one OR gate.
example.work: A 2-to-4 active-high decoder gives Y0 = A'B', Y1 = A'B, Y2 = AB' and Y3 = AB. The function needs m1 and m2, so OR Y1 and Y2.
example.answer: f = Y1 + Y2 = A'B + AB' = A XOR B. One decoder and one two-input OR gate.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.49 wires a 2-to-4 decoder's outputs into a 4-to-1 multiplexer and asks how many of the 16 input combinations give Y = 1 - a decoder question and a multiplexer question at once, answerable only by writing the decoder outputs as minterms first. GATE CSE 2014 Set 2 Q.7 asks what a counter plus a decoder is, which is the one-hot property.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A 3-to-8 active-high decoder and a single 4-input OR gate are to implement f = m0 + m3 + m5 + m6. What is the gate count, and what changes if the decoder's outputs are active-low?
variations.answer: One decoder and one 4-input OR gate for active-high outputs; for active-low outputs the OR becomes a 4-input NAND.
variations.why: Each decoder output is one minterm, so the function is the OR of four of them. With active-low outputs each line is the complement of its minterm, and De Morgan turns the OR of complements into the NAND of the lines.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: How many 3-to-8 decoders with enable are needed to build a 5-to-32 decoder, and what drives their enables?
variations.answer: Five: four to produce the 32 outputs and one to decode the two top address bits into the four enables.
variations.why: 32 outputs need 32 / 8 = 4 blocks, and those blocks must be enabled one at a time by the two remaining address bits, which a small decoder does. The bottom three address bits go to all four blocks in parallel.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Which outputs of a 3-to-8 decoder must be ORed to realise f = A XOR B XOR C?
variations.answer: Y1, Y2, Y4 and Y7 - the minterms 001, 010, 100 and 111, which are exactly the codes with an odd number of 1s.
variations.why: The three-input XOR is 1 for an odd count of ones, so its minterms are 1, 2, 4 and 7. The decoder supplies each of them on one line, and the OR collects them.

trap.what: Forgetting the polarity of the decoder outputs and ORing active-low lines as if they were minterms.
trap.why: An active-low decoder asserts 0 on the selected line, so the selected line is the complement of the minterm. ORing them gives the complement of what you want, and the circuit is wrong for every input.
trap.counterexample: With an active-low 2-to-4 decoder, ORing the lines for m1 and m2 gives (A'B)' + (AB')' = A + B' + A' + B = 1, a constant 1 instead of A XOR B. The correct gate is a NAND of those two lines.

check.question: A 3-to-8 decoder is used with one 8-input OR gate. How many distinct functions of three variables can that arrangement realise?
check.explanation: There are 2^3 = 8 decoder lines, one per minterm, and a function is fixed by choosing which of them to OR. That is 2^8 = 256 choices, which is exactly the number of Boolean functions of three variables.
